seoTitle: Change Your Domain Name in Squarespace (2026)
metaDescription: Point a new or existing domain to your Squarespace website, whether you're buying one through Squarespace or connecting one you already own.
intro: Whether you're rebranding or just picking a better web address, changing the domain pointed at your Squarespace site is a straightforward process. This guide covers both buying a new domain through Squarespace and connecting one you already own from another registrar.

steps.heading: Log in to Squarespace
steps.body: Sign in to your account, using Google, a work email, or Apple/Facebook via More Options if you're setting up new.

steps.heading: Open Domains and Email
steps.body: From your dashboard's left panel, click Settings, then hover over Domains and Email to see your options.

steps.heading: Register a new domain or use an existing one
steps.body: Click Get a Domain to search and purchase one through Squarespace, or enter a domain you already own to check availability and connect it.

steps.heading: Point the domain to Squarespace
steps.body: Once your domain is added, change it to point to your Squarespace site so it becomes your site's live web address.

steps.heading: Check the SSL and domain details
steps.body: Click on the connected domain to view details including SSL certificate status, then confirm it's set as your site's primary domain.

faq.question: Can I use a domain I already bought elsewhere?
faq.answer: Yes, you can enter your existing domain and connect it to point to your Squarespace site instead of buying a new one.

faq.question: How much does a domain cost through Squarespace?
faq.answer: Prices vary by domain and extension, so check availability and pricing when you search for the one you want.

faq.question: Will my SSL certificate update automatically with a new domain?
faq.answer: Squarespace manages SSL for connected domains, and you can check its status from the domain details page.

faq.question: Does changing my domain affect my existing site content?
faq.answer: No, changing the domain only affects the web address pointing to your site — your pages and design stay the same.
